x: And Geoff Dearman (4x400m), Matt Douglas (400m hurdles) and Stuart Faben (javelin) gained selection for the European U23 championships. Last year's very welcome improving trend over the country has continued.
First Stuart Clark in the long jump and then Matt Douglas in both hurdles contributed valuable points. So too did Matt Simson, winning the 'A' shot in his first competition for Belgrave.

The ever reliable Matt Douglas coasted home to win the 'B' 400H in relaxed style. Good points in the 800 from Matt Yates and a slightly injured Darrell Maynard and we looked to be on course for a big score.
Matt Douglas and Noel Levy got us off to a good start in the 400H and immediately afterwards Tom Lerwill and Dave Pamah provided near maximum points in the 800m, so already things were looking good.

The big improvements in: the Shot (Matt Simpson), 3000 Steeplechase (Justin Chaston and Lee Hurst), High Jump (Brendan Reilly), 5000 (Paul Evans), and 400H (Matt Douglas), show how big points can be accumulated by key individuals.

Another solid performance from Matt Douglas earned him the bronze medal spot in the long hurdles and this, followed by Tom Lerwill's gun to tape victory in the 800m , moved us into numero uno position – which we were not to relinquish all afternoon.

Matt Douglas looked the class act in the 400m hurdles, coasting to a 1.5 second victory over Haringey's Lawrence Lynch. Matt Kloiber jetted down from holiday in Scotland to strengthen our middle distance squad and sat on Tony Whiteman as the pair raced through 400m in 52 and bits.
Enfield, 3rd May 1997 and Matt Douglas finds himself sandwiched between Lloyd Cowan (Shaftesbury Barnet) on the far side and Kirk Harries (Puma TVH).  Matt came home 3rd in 14.68.

…on Lobo over 800m, Dave Smith in the hammer and Ian Tullett in the pole vault – all of these in the English team – plus Matt Douglas for Northern Ireland in the 400m hurdles, Lee Newman in the discus for Wales and Dave Pamah in the 1500m for St.…
Selection for this Under 23 International resulted in a super 6-man Belgrave representation with wins coming from Geoff Dearman and Matt Douglas.

Over the barriers, a lifetime best came from Northern Ireland's Matt Douglas in the one-lap race and Andy Tulloch continued his comeback from injury with a super 13.57, his best of the year, to reach the final where he placed 6th.

Castro of Sporting Club of Lisbon got outkicked as James succumbed to the heat and travelling and faded serenely to 6th spot. Matt Douglas struggled to find form in the 400H as Kevin Young cruised to 48.88 at the age of 32.
Matt Douglas nudged towards his PB in his first outing of the year while Ian Wells pointed out that his 'B' selection was the first by right for three years.
Matt Douglas clocked the same time as in Match 1 to win the 'A' 400H. Darren Campbell and Jason Fergus ensured good points in the 100 but a poor start cost Darren victory.
